dataset: Kaggle FF++ C23, xdxd003/ff-c23, dataset version 1
limitations: One training seed; source-pair splits do not prove identity-disjoint generalization.
FF++ facial manipulations do not establish detection of fully AI-generated videos.
Warm inference excludes model loading; filesystem page cache may be warm.
If resumed_videos is nonzero, completed video measurements were checksummed and retained across sessions with identical code/settings/runtime.
Optional Drive recovery I/O runs between videos and is excluded from inference latency; source media are still decoded afresh for every arm/repeat.
Approximate pHash reuse can miss short or subtle edits; compare against fusion_all.

metric_notes.calibration: ECE/Brier measure error; no calibration fitted on test data.
metric_notes.energy_and_utilization: Not measured; GPU power/utilization polling would perturb wall timing.
metric_notes.frame_level: Correlated descriptive metrics only; confidence intervals use video source groups, never frames.
metric_notes.gpu_memory: PyTorch allocator peak includes all resident comparator models; excludes CUDA context/non-Torch allocations.
metric_notes.rss: Process RSS snapshot, not total runtime/decoder-worker peak RAM.

proof_limit: Hashes establish that later files match this recorded bundle. Public-chain anchoring adds a tamper-evident timestamp after deployment; neither proves dataset authenticity or model truthfulness.
scope: 100 selected held-out videos out of a 240-video test pool; 18 real and 82 manipulated; three timing repeats per arm
title: Authenfy EfficientNet fusion v1: 100-video FF++ C23 benchmark
verification: Recompute every files.*.sha256 value and compare evidence.json.sha256; an Ethereum AnalysisRegistry anchor can timestamp the benchmark.json hash and this manifest hash.
